title: Optimize quantized kernels: INT8/FP8 smoothquant + dequant fusion + KV cache + continuous batching
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Performance: Improved throughput for INT8/FP8 quantized models via fused smoothquant+dequant kernels and KV-cache copy reduction; Scheduling: continuous-batching policy change increases GPU utilization; Stability: fixes edge case in FP8 scale handling.
description:
Context and motivation:
We have multiple customer and benchmark signals showing that quantized inference (INT8/FP8) is a critical path for cost-sensitive workloads, but current runtime inefficiencies around dequantization, smoothquant scaling, KV cache copies, and scheduling result in suboptimal throughput and tail latency. This PR implements a set of coordinated changes (kernel fusion, memory layout adjustments, and scheduler tuning) to reduce per-token overhead and improve steady-state throughput under continuous batching workloads.

Summary of changes:
- Implement fused smoothquant + dequant + matmul output path for INT8 and FP8 kernels to eliminate intermediate dequantization copies and extra element-wise ops (new kernels in src/runtime/kernels/quant_fused.cc).
- Add FP8 scale/metadata propagation to the fused kernels and fix an FP8 edge-case where near-zero scales caused NaNs in cast paths.
- Optimize KV cache layout and copy-on-write paths to avoid an extra host->device memcpy during cache growth (src/runtime/cache/kv_cache.cu).
- Introduce a continuous-batching scheduler variant that maintains small resident batches and uses dynamic microbatch sizing to lower p99 latency while improving throughput for bursty request patterns (src/runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cpp).
- Add a small microbenchmark harness and integration tests for fused kernels (tests/perf/quant_fused_bench.cc, tests/integration/quant_kv_integration_test.py).
- Add telemetry: per-kernel token timings and a new perf metric (quant_fused_ops) surfaced to the Console.

Why this approach:
Fusing smoothquant + dequant into the matmul epilogue removes an intermediate tensor and the dequant op, which is costly for INT8/FP8 conversions. Combined with a KV cache layout that avoids ephemeral device copies, we cut both compute and memory-transfer overhead. Continuous-batching scheduler changes improve token-level batching efficiency without harming tail latency for low-QPS customers.

Benchmarks (A100, sequence=1024, batch steady-state):
- Baseline (current main): throughput = 1000 tokens/s, p95 latency = 28 ms
- With fused kernels + KV layout + continuous batching: throughput = 1180 tokens/s (+18%), p95 latency = 24.8 ms (-11.4%), p99 latency = 42 ms (-8%).
- INT8-specific microbenchmark: single-node throughput +22% vs baseline quant path.
- FP8 path: throughput +12% and stable numeric results across eval prompt set (more details in artifacts).

Compatibility and safety:
- All fused kernels are behind a runtime feature flag (quant_fused_kernel=true) and fall back to the existing dequant path when disabled.
- Added comprehensive numerics checks (unit tests) to ensure bitwise-consistent FP32 fallback where required by customers.
- No API changes. Config knobs: quant_fused_kernel, continuous_batcher.enabled, kvcache.copy_on_write=false to toggle the memory path.

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for fused kernels and FP8 scale handling.
- Integration tests for KV cache correctness on multi-turn chat workloads.
- Regression tests against a curated eval set (prompt set v2026-02) to ensure quality parity.
- CI: linux-gcc build, cuda tests on A100 runners, Python integration matrix. All CI checks passed after two iterations.

Risk and rollout plan:
- Rollout is staged: by default the feature flag is off for hosted API. Gradual enablement in internal perf clusters, then canary to 5% of traffic, then wider rollout. We will monitor quant_fused_ops and token-level errors as rollout guards.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel implementation with unit tests
- [x] KV cache layout and integration tests
- [x] Scheduler changes + end-to-end perf harness
- [x] Benchmarks attached (artifacts/perf/905321/*)
